newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo debt deal to be signed on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo debt deal to be signed on Wednesday.

text.p: Finance Ministry officials will be in Sao Paulo this morning to sign a debt refinancing deal with Sao Paulo state, including its debts owed to state bank Banespa, officials said.

The deal would involve the payment of 20 percent of Sao Paulo's 37 billion real debt through asset sales, while the remainder would be refinanced over 30 years paying interest per year of six percent plus inflation.
The refinancing package also would include the transfer of Sao Paulo state's controlling stake in Banespa to the federal government.
Gazeta Mercantil financial newspaper said an independent manager is likely to be hired to run Banespa for one year and ready it for possible privatization.
Sao Paulo state will have the chance to regain control of Banespa once it pays off 50 percent of its 20 billion real debt with the bank.
To recover the bank, Banespa would have to pay a further 6.0 billion to 7.0 billion reais with the sell-off of assets, the newspaper said.
Banespa, Brazil's largest state bank, has been under Central Bank management since December 1994 due to Sao Paulo's massive debt with it.

Trade in Banespa shares was suspended on Tuesday amid expectations over the deal and following a request by Brazil's Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM) and the stock exchanges for clarification on a press report that the bank had a 786.3 million real net profit in the first nine months.
Banespa preferred stock rose over 160 percent in eight sessions before it was suspended.
